chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn al-Mubarik said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the charity of al-Fitr (Zakat al-Fitr): is it from what Allah the Exalted said, 'Establish the prayer and give the zakat'? He said, 'Yes.' And he said, 'The charity of dates is more beloved to me because my father (peace be upon him) used to give charity in dates.' I said, 'If one assigns its value as silver and gives it to one man or two?' He said, 'Distributing it is more beloved to me, and there is no harm in making it silver, but dates are more beloved to me.' I said, 'Should I give it to those who are not from the Ahl al-Wilayah among these neighbors?' He said, 'Yes, the neighbors are more entitled to it.' I said, 'Should I give the one man three sa' and four sa'?' He said, 'Yes.'

The meaning in this hadith is that if there is a group of needy people, distributing among them is superior to giving it to one person. As for if there is no necessity, the best is to give a head (share) to each head, even though in the report, in his saying 'Distributing it is more beloved to me,' it does not mean that one must distribute one head to one individual individually. It is possible that he meant those upon whom the Fitr is obligatory, so that he distributes and gives each one of them a head is superior to giving it to one man. And on this interpretation, there is no contradiction between this report and the first report, and we have clarified in the first report that there is no harm in giving one man many heads. And to add clarification to this is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَهْلُ اَلْوِلَايَة: Ahl al-Wilayah (the family of the Prophet and their descendants)
key_terms.رَأْس: Head (referring to an individual share or portion)
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ اَلْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr (charity of breaking the fast)
key_terms.صِيْع: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for distributing Zakat al-Fitr among the poor?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that Zakat al-Fitr falls under the general Quranic command of 'giving Zakat,' establishing its scriptural basis. While he prefers the traditional medium of dates, he permits monetary valuation, emphasizing that distribution among multiple recipients is superior to concentrating it on one, unless necessity dictates otherwise. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maximizing benefit to the needy while maintaining flexibility in the form of payment.
